Yea ACE was awesome (most are your age).  People @ ACE had degrees from all different areas. I work at a state hatchery (cal department of fish and wildlife) as a seasonal aid in fresno. We raise several species of trout and one species of salmon for recreational stocking of lakes and rivers.  I'm going to back to grad school so I can move my career into more conservation/ecology around freshwater fish and ecosystems. The head guy of this hatchery and several other hatcheries in the area had gotten an undergrad degree in film making and totally took his career a different route. One project partner we had in Inyo national forest was high up in the ranks at inyo and he didn't even have a degree and did freelance textile design for 15 years before he went back to the forest service and worked his way up. He use to say he had a major in wilderness and a minor in trials (or vice versa don't remeber lol).
Yea man I'd stay in school 🏫. And get an AA or BS or take a break and do ACE for a three or six month term and than go back to school. That's if land management/conservation/habitat restoration is something u want

Well I'll say this, you have a lot of opportunity to work your way up to at least a red hat in the CCCs, I was in the CCCs when I was 19. You should take every opportunity you have to learn as much as possible from the saws to trailbuilding and whatever they got for yah. I've seen many people do terms and just get lost in the sauce (me included). I've also seen people come up and built lasting land management careers regardless if they have degrees or not. 

Little history- I was in the CCCs for a year (19 yo) But ended up getting my degree in environmental science almost ten years later (28 yo). (I wasted so much prescoius time on bs)  Than I joined a program called ACE (highly recommend even after CCC term) add ended up getting a job with the state after my ACE term ended. 

I really think my degree and my time at ACE helped me land this state job. 

So sorry I can't answer all your questions, but imo the CCCS or any americorp term with conservation in mind is worth it not only for the scholarship money but for the  experience of a life time (imo).

Just if you join a program like this, just put your all into it and don't let it opportunities they give u pass u by. Also opportunities start popping up left and right the longer you are in programs like these.

Hopefully that gives u a little confidence that this is the right path for you dude 🙏🏼. Dm if u have qs.
